items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: So Cosy who could copy things from records and write them, wrote my parts in the keys they were supposed to be in and I had no troubles after that.

ctx.x: The next day we started rehearsing the show which included six acts with a troupe of English girls and a tap dancer named Rosalind Wade. A French trombonist who had been in Bombay for sometime was added to the orchestra which made ten musicians in the orchestra. We opened a couple of days later and everything went fine. Arthur Lanier sang ballads and we formed a quartet with Leon, Ollie Tines, Lanier and myself to sing variety numbers. The job was not hard because we worked 4 nights and 2 matinees a week.

The management found two apartments for us. Leon with Boop, Cosy, Lanie, Beezie and myself stayed in a six-room apartment called Moby Mansion. Charlie Lewis and Ollie Tines were in an apartment not far from where we lived with their Anglo-Indian girl friends whom they had met during their first stay in Bombay. Cricket Smith and Rudy Jackson lived with their Anglo-Indian women. Leonard, a French trombone player who had been added to the band, had been in India for some years and lived with some friends. We also…

Some of the acts that we played in the Taj did not have their music arranged to suit the formation of the orchestra and had no parts for trumpets. So they gave Cricket and I violin parts to transpose. I was not up to date on transposing because I had never had to do it, but Cricket could transpose as if it had been actually written for a trumpet
